title: Choking
description: An object is blocking the airway. The person cannot breathe, speak, or cough effectively.

recognition_questions.q: Is the person able to speak, cough, or breathe?
Are they clutching their throat (universal choking sign)?

immediate_safety_warnings: If the person becomes unconscious, lower them carefully to the ground and start CPR.
Do not leave the person alone to find help if they are conscious — call 112 on speaker.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Ask 'Are you choking?'. If they cannot speak, cough, or breathe, act immediately.

ordered_instructions.rationale: Emergency services are needed if back blows fail.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Lean the person forward. Give 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Back blows can dislodge the obstruction.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If still blocked, give 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich): stand behind, place a fist above the navel, grasp with the other hand, pull sharply inward and upward.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Abdominal thrusts push air from the lungs to expel the object.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is dislodged or the person becomes unconscious.
If the person becomes unconscious, lower them carefully, start CPR. Check the mouth before rescue breaths.

actions_to_avoid: Do NOT do abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year — use chest thrusts instead.
Do not do back blows or abdominal thrusts if the person can still cough forcefully — encourage them to cough.
Do not perform a blind finger sweep — you may push the object deeper.
Do not give food or water.

escalation_conditions.condition: Object not dislodged after 3 cycles of back blows + abdominal thrusts
Person was given abdominal thrusts (even if successful)
escalation_conditions.action: They must be assessed in hospital for internal injury

approved_alternatives.alternative: Chest thrusts for a pregnant or obese person: place hands on the lower half of the breastbone and thrust inward

follow_up_requirements: Anyone who received abdominal thrusts must see a doctor to check for internal injury.

age_specific_pathways.infant: Use 5 back blows (infant face-down along your forearm, head lower than chest) then 5 chest thrusts (two fingers on the lower breastbone). Repeat. Do NOT use abdominal thrusts.
age_specific_pathways.child: Same technique as adult but use less force. Kneel to be at the child's height.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
